liebermann.notes: A miscellany of fragments; f. 42 is a scraped, holed and stained former wrapper bearing a fragment of Af–Ine (Ine Pr–23), with Kentish traces in the language.

entries.text_de:
British Museum Burney 277, ein Miscellanband verschiedenster Fragmente. Darin f. 42, um 1030, ein Pergamentbogen, einstiger Heftumschlag, verschabt, durchlöchert, befleckt, schwer lesbar, Fragment von Af-Ine, nämlich Ine Pr—23, u. S. 88.

Der Text zeigt Kentische Spuren: z. B. Ine 16 geceþan; 17 ofspereð; 21, 1 remeð; 3 werce.
entries.text_en:
British Museum Burney 277, a miscellany of the most varied fragments. In it f. 42, c. 1030, a parchment sheet, once a quire wrapper, rubbed, holed, stained, hard to read: a fragment of Af-Ine, namely Ine Pr—23, below, p. 88.

The text shows Kentish traces: e.g. Ine 16 geceþan; 17 ofspereð; 21, 1 remeð; 3 werce.

wormald.shelfmark: London, British Library, Burney MS 277, f. 42
wormald.wormald_date: s. xi² (script, after Ker), p. 257 n. 357; Table 4.1, p. 165
wormald.wormald_origin: Origin unknown ('???', Table 4.1). Dialect called 'Kentish', or at least south-eastern (p. 257). Used for pen-trials before and during the 13th century; the parent MS was presumably broken up about then and the bifolium became a wrapper (p. 257 and n. 358).
wormald.laws: Ine (last words of Ine Prol. to end of Ine 23), from the Alfred–Ine law-book
wormald.other_contents: None surviving. A single bifolium (leaves 207 × 130 mm), the central bifolium of a quire, giving four continuous pages (c. 100 lines, 25 to the page); modest initials (Ine's first law enlarged in red and black, others red or black, two ornamented Gs). Later a wrapper (letter 'S', perhaps 'B', visible on its spine).
wormald.overview: A battered bifolium of the second half of the eleventh century, with four consecutive pages from Alfred and Ine's law-book, running from the close of Ine's prologue to Ine 23, in a dialect described as Kentish or at least south-eastern. Its text differs in a few respects from that of Corpus 383 and the uncorrected Textus Roffensis. Space calculations suggest that the parent MS did not hold the law-book alone; Wormald notes that it comes closest in date, size and look to Nero A.i(A) and may have been an MS of that kind. It survived because it was reused as a wrapper, probably in the thirteenth century.
wormald.key_quote: 'it is worth pondering that it is nearest in date, size and general appearance to Nero A.i(A)' (p. 258)
wormald.doubts: GUIDE: the guide's 'Laws in it' gives 'Af, Ine', but the fragment contains Ine only (Ine Prol.–23); Af would have stood in the lost part of the parent book. GUIDE: Liebermann's date c. 1030 differs from Wormald/Ker's s. xi² (p. 257 n. 357). Textual differences: lacks the additions to Ine 3:1–2 found in Corpus 383 and inserted in TR; variants at Ine 6:3, 6:5, 8, 21 and archaic dual 'twædne' in Ine 23 (n. 359). Ker, Catalogue no. 136.
verify_notes: overview: 'represents a separate line of transmission' went beyond Wormald (p. 257 says only that the text is distinct in a couple of respects; n. 359 compares pre-correction TR); 'show' softened to 'suggest' since the space argument is conditional (p. 258).
pages: Table 4.1 entry is on p. 165 only.
overview: reworded to remove five-word runs shared with Wormald.

laws_note.text: Ine only (from the end of Ine Prol. to Ine 23); Alfred’s laws would have stood in the lost part of the MS.
